ip_top_stories.title: Publishers Back Concord Music Group's AI Suit Against Anthropic
ip_top_stories.summary: Publishers and media groups have filed in support of Concord Music Group's copyright lawsuit against Anthropic. The case centres on allegations that the AI company used copyrighted musical works without authorisation in training its models. The backing from publishers signals a broadening coalition of content owners challenging AI training practices.

ip_top_stories.title: Penguin to Sue OpenAI Over ChatGPT Version of German Children's Book
ip_top_stories.summary: A German children's book publisher is suing OpenAI over allegations that ChatGPT reproduced content from a copyrighted children's book without authorisation. The case is among the latest European publisher actions targeting AI companies for copyright infringement. Multiple sources cover the story; the most direct report is via Reuters.

ip_top_stories.title: Anthropic's Amodei Seeks Copyright Deal That 'Works for Everyone'
ip_top_stories.summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has publicly called for a copyright framework that balances the interests of AI developers and creators, speaking in the context of an Australian copyright dispute. His comments come as Anthropic faces multiple infringement lawsuits globally. The intervention signals the company's preference for negotiated licensing over litigation outcomes.

ip_top_stories.title: French Private Members' Bill Aims to Protect Creatives' Copyright from AI Usage
ip_top_stories.summary: A private members' bill has been introduced in the French parliament seeking to protect creators' copyright from unauthorised use in AI training. The proposal reflects growing legislative pressure across Europe to address gaps in existing copyright law as it applies to generative AI. France joins a number of jurisdictions actively considering or enacting AI-specific copyright protections.

ip_top_stories.title: What AI Asks of Open Access
ip_top_stories.summary: The Scholarly Kitchen examines how the rise of AI training on openly accessible research content is challenging the assumptions underpinning open access publishing. The piece explores whether open access licences were designed to accommodate large-scale AI ingestion, and what obligations—if any—AI developers have to the scholarly publishing ecosystem. It raises important questions about the sustainability of open access in an AI-driven environment.

ip_further_links.title: UK Government Maintains Status Quo on AI and Copyright, Playing the Long Game on Potential Reform
ip_further_links.summary: The UK government has signalled it will not rush AI copyright reform, instead taking a cautious approach while monitoring developments in litigation and international policy.

ip_further_links.title: Q&A: The UK's Copyright Report – A Gift to Creators, A Problem for AI
ip_further_links.summary: A legal Q&A examines the implications of the UK's recent copyright report for AI developers and rights holders, noting tensions between creator protections and AI innovation.

ip_further_links.title: Cloudflare Legal Chief on AI Bots and Publisher Revenue Loss
ip_further_links.summary: Cloudflare's chief legal officer discusses the impact of AI crawlers on publisher revenue and the company's approach to managing bot traffic and piracy orders.

ip_further_links.title: How African Creators Are Currently Being Exploited in the AI Boom
ip_further_links.summary: An investigation details how African creators' works are being ingested into AI training datasets without consent or compensation, highlighting gaps in global copyright enforcement.

ip_further_links.title: Is Copyright Law the Wrong Weapon Against AI?
ip_further_links.summary: A commentary piece questions whether copyright litigation is the most effective legal tool for addressing harms caused by AI training, and considers alternative regulatory approaches.

ip_further_links.title: How India Is Trying to Navigate AI Copyright's Three-Body Problem
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis of India's evolving approach to AI copyright, examining the competing interests of AI developers, rights holders, and users in shaping national policy.

ip_further_links.title: Harlequin to Co-Produce AI-Generated 'Microdramas'
ip_further_links.summary: Publisher Harlequin has announced plans to co-produce a slate of AI-generated short-form video content, raising questions about AI's role in mainstream publishing and content creation.

ip_further_links.title: Media Bosses: 'Australia Shouldn't Be Held to Ransom' by AI Giants
ip_further_links.summary: Australian media executives have called for stronger government action to prevent AI companies from exploiting local publishers' content without payment or negotiation.

ip_further_links.title: Beyond Copyright: Why Asia Pacific Governments Must Govern AI Training Data as Public Infrastructure
ip_further_links.summary: A policy commentary argues that Asia Pacific governments should treat AI training data governance as a matter of public infrastructure rather than relying solely on copyright law.

ip_further_links.title: AI Law in Canada Is Evolving Through Familiar Principles
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis of how Canadian courts and regulators are applying existing legal principles to AI copyright and liability questions, in the absence of comprehensive AI-specific legislation.
